System, developer, user, and repository instructions take precedence.\\n\\nAttn delegation starts a separate agent session the user can inspect and steer. Start one when authorized by the user or the assigned task. Before delegating, read the delegation reference in the `attn` skill.\\n\\nUse Attn's configured roles and model choices by default. Honor an explicit user request to use a different role or model for a delegation without changing saved settings.\\n\\nIf standing guidance in AGENTS.md, skills, or other instruction files conflicts with Attn's configuration, explain the specific conflict and ask the user which should govern.\\n\\nA subagent is a native runtime subagent that reports to its calling agent. An Attn delegation is a separate session.\\n\\nattn keeps work as seeds in your profile's garden. A seed belongs to its planting profile for life. Lists, links, children, claims and delegations stay in that profile; another profile's seed is refused by name. Inside attn, your session chooses the profile. Outside attn, use `--profile \u003cname|id\u003e` when several profiles exist; a single profile is selected automatically. A seed is one unit of work: a short id like `s-7k3f9m`, a slug like `mermaid-rendered-grid` (the title's first key words), a title, a markdown body, a state. The id is for commands and for other agents; every verb prints it beside the slug. To the user, say the slug: `mermaid-rendered-grid` (`s-7k3f9m`) on first mention, then the slug alone. A person should never have to decode an id.\\n\\nWrite every seed body as a work prompt for an agent starting without this conversation, including work you plan to do yourself. State the task and outcome, starting context and constraints, and how to verify completion.\\n\\nA plot is a seed with children: its body records the shared plan, and each child has its own work prompt. Keep shared decisions in the parent; tell each child which parent section, sibling result or artifact to read and why. Related bodies are not included automatically in a delegation. Children are parallel unless a `blocks` edge orders them. Read `attn seed guide` before writing a plot. Any seed can be a plot. Seed packets are templates for plots; the attn skill explains them.\\n\\nGarden words have Jira-style equivalents: seed = ticket, ready = todo, plot = epic, harvested = done. Use the Garden word by default. When the user uses one of those Jira words, mirror it for that concept for the rest of the exchange; do not correct them, and do not switch the other concepts unless they do.\\n\\nTrack work that outlives this turn in seeds, not in markdown TODO lists or your harness's todo tool, which end with the session: a bug you found, a follow-up you are not doing now, a piece you split off. Search before you plant: `attn seed search \u003cwords\u003e` reads every title, body and log in the garden, harvested and withered seeds included, so you find work that already exists instead of planting it twice. Plant work before you start it, so the claim and the log exist while you work. Under a plot, plant with `--part-of \u003cplot\u003e` so it stays with its plan. If you discover work while tending another seed, add `--discovered-from \u003cseed\u003e` so its origin is on record. Before your turn ends, plant what is still undone. Harvest a seed when the outcome and required verification in its body are complete.\\n\\nA delegation assigns its seed to the new agent as their stake: the seed they tend and report to. A new delegation stores its brief as the seed body. A delegation at an existing seed uses that body's assignment. The opening identifies the seed; the agent reads its current body and notes. Handover saves the next-step note and transfers ownership before starting a new agent, leaving the previous session running. `attn seed ready` without flags shows your stake's plot. When a session delegates more work, a new brief becomes a child only when the resolved source has a stake. Every other garden verb uses the seed id you provide.\\n\\nThe loop:\\n\\n    attn seed ready                  what you can pick up now: open, not parked, not blocked, nobody claiming it\\n                                     inside your plot when you report to one. A plot itself is never ready; only its children can be\\n    attn seed ready --all            the same across your profile's garden; use it to look past your plot\\n    attn seed show \u003cid\u003e              body, state, tender, edges, children, freshest handoff\\n    attn seed tend \u003cid\u003e              claim it; one tender at a time, a claimed seed refuses you by name\\n    attn seed note \u003cid\u003e -m \\\"…\\\"       what happened and what you learned, tending it or not; --handoff addresses the next tender\\n                                     --ring tells watchers to look\\n    attn seed check report \u003cid\u003e \u003cC#\u003e -m \\\"…\\\" --evidence \u003cartifact|url\u003e    the proof for one of the seed's checks; `attn seed --help` has the other check verbs\\n    attn seed harvest \u003cid\u003e -m \\\"…\\\"    done; the reason is required and fits in 400 characters, the long version goes in a note\\n    attn seed harvest \u003cid\u003e --when-merged [pr-url]    only when a merge is all that is left: the seed lets go and harvests itself when that pull request merges\\n                                     with no url it takes this session's single open pull request; --when-merged --clear takes the arming back\\n    attn seed wither \u003cid\u003e [-m \\\"…\\\"]   abandoned, nobody will pick it up\\n    attn seed park \u003cid\u003e              put down, claim released; tend it again to resume\\n    attn seed replant \u003cid\u003e           a harvested or withered seed back to planted\\n    attn seed search \u003cwords\u003e         find seeds by keyword across your profile's garden, closed ones included; the line that\\n                                     matched prints under each hit. Run it before you plant\\n    attn seed plant \\\"\u003ctitle\u003e\\\" -m \\\"…\\\" [--part-of \u003cplot\u003e] [--discovered-from \u003cseed\u003e]    a new seed; prints the id\\n\\n`tend`, `park`, `harvest`, `wither` and `replant` refuse a seed that another agent claims, and name that agent. Add `--force` to do it anyway. The log records that you forced it. A session's claim ends when the session ends. A crew member, a permanent agent, keeps their claim across sessions. `attn seed tend \u003cid\u003e --for \u003cname\u003e` gives a seed to a crew member. The user never claims seeds.\\n\\n`harvest` and `wither` print the seeds they unblock and ring those seeds' tenders and watchers, as `--ring` does for a note.\\n\\nPlans:\\n\\n    attn seed plot -f \u003cfile.json\u003e    a whole plot in one move; - reads stdin. The file is\\n                                     {\\\"title\\\": …, \\\"body\\\": …, \\\"children\\\": [{\\\"title\\\": …, \\\"body\\\": …, \\\"blocks\\\": [\\\"\u003csibling-slug\u003e\\\"]}]}\\n                                     A slug is the sibling's title without its stop words, lowercased and dash-joined; writing the sibling's title works too. `attn seed guide` has a full example\\n    attn seed link \u003ca\u003e blocks \u003cb\u003e    b waits until a closes; unlink removes the edge\\n    attn seed link \u003ca\u003e part-of \u003cb\u003e   a joins b's plot; a seed sits in one plot at a time\\n    attn seed link \u003ca\u003e discovered-from \u003cb\u003e    a was discovered while working on b; the link records that origin but never orders or blocks anything\\n    attn seed ls [--flat]            everything planted and who tends it, children nested under their plot; --flat for one list\\n    attn seed edit \u003cid\u003e -m \\\"…\\\"       replace the body; say what changed in a note\\n\\nKeeping up:\\n\\nWhen attn sends an update notification, run the suggested command to read it. Reading acknowledges the update and maintains awareness; it does not authorize or require acting on the update. Only act or interrupt the user when attention is genuinely needed.\\n\\n    attn seed notes \u003cid\u003e             the whole log, newest first\\n    attn seed watch \u003cid\u003e             watch this seed and its descendants; unwatch removes this subscription\\n    attn seed attach \u003cid\u003e --path \u003cfile\u003e (--move | --copy)    bring a local file into durable seed ownership; Move is recommended\\n    attn seed detach \u003cid\u003e --path \u003cfilename\u003e --to \u003cdestination\u003e    move an owned file back out without overwriting\\n    attn seed attach \u003cid\u003e --path \u003cfile\u003e --repo \u003crepo\u003e | --notebook \u003cdoc-id\u003e | --url \u003curl\u003e    keep a link to a document elsewhere\\n    attn seed export \u003cid\u003e [--out \u003cpath\u003e]    the seed and its log as one markdown file\\n\\nEvery delegation, including a handover, makes both the delegate and the agent that delegated watch the seed and its descendants. A crew member's watch lasts across their sessions. `unwatch` removes that watch. Watches on the seed's children or ancestors stay. `show` and `unwatch` list the watches still covering a seed and how to remove each. To watch again, run `watch` or delegate the seed again. Restarting or resuming the delegation does not bring a removed watch back.\\n\\nUse attn agent msg for attn-managed sessions; keep Claude's SendMessage for follow-ups to the native subagents this session spawned.\\n\\n`attn session rename \\\"\u003ca few words\u003e\\\" [--session \u003cid\u003e]` renames a session, yours by default, when its main work drifts from the name it started with.\\n\\n`attn seed --help` has every flag. `attn seed guide` has how to write a body worth handing to somebody else.\"","-C","/tmp/work","--","Task λ {{literal}}\nsecond line"]

A new delegation stores its brief as the seed body. A delegation at an existing seed uses that body's assignment. The opening identifies the seed; the agent reads its current body and notes. Handover saves the next-step note and transfers ownership before starting a new agent, leaving the previous session running. `attn seed ready` without flags shows your stake's plot. When a session delegates more work, a new brief becomes a child only when the resolved source has a stake. Every other garden verb uses the seed id you provide.\\n\\nThe loop:\\n\\n    attn seed ready                  what you can pick up now: open, not parked, not blocked, nobody claiming it\\n                                     inside your plot when you report to one. Lists, links, children, claims and delegations stay in that profile; another profile's seed is refused by name. Inside attn, your session chooses the profile. Outside attn, use `--profile \u003cname|id\u003e` when several profiles exist; a single profile is selected automatically. A seed is one unit of work: a short id like `s-7k3f9m`, a slug like `mermaid-rendered-grid` (the title's first key words), a title, a markdown body, a state. The id is for commands and for other agents; every verb prints it beside the slug. To the user, say the slug: `mermaid-rendered-grid` (`s-7k3f9m`) on first mention, then the slug alone. State the task and outcome, starting context and constraints, and how to verify completion.\\n\\nA plot is a seed with children: its body records the shared plan, and each child has its own work prompt. Keep shared decisions in the parent; tell each child which parent section, sibling result or artifact to read and why. Related bodies are not included automatically in a delegation. Seed packets are templates for plots; the attn skill explains them.\\n\\nGarden words have Jira-style equivalents: seed = ticket, ready = todo, plot = epic, harvested = done. Use the Garden word by default. When the user uses one of those Jira words, mirror it for that concept for the rest of the exchange; do not correct them, and do not switch the other concepts unless they do.\\n\\nTrack work that outlives this turn in seeds, not in markdown TODO lists or your harness's todo tool, which end with the session: a bug you found, a follow-up you are not doing now, a piece you split off. Search before you plant: `attn seed search \u003cwords\u003e` reads every title, body and log in the garden, harvested and withered seeds included, so you find work that already exists instead of planting it twice. Plant work before you start it, so the claim and the log exist while you work. Under a plot, plant with `--part-of \u003cplot\u003e` so it stays with its plan. If you discover work while tending another seed, add `--discovered-from \u003cseed\u003e` so its origin is on record. Before your turn ends, plant what is still undone. Harvest a seed when the outcome and required verification in its body are complete.\\n\\nA delegation assigns its seed to the new agent as their stake: the seed they tend and report to. A new delegation stores its brief as the seed body. A delegation at an existing seed uses that body's assignment. The opening identifies the seed; the agent reads its current body and notes. Handover saves the next-step note and transfers ownership before starting a new agent, leaving the previous session running. `attn seed ready` without flags shows your stake's plot. When a session delegates more work, a new brief becomes a child only when the resolved source has a stake. Every other garden verb uses the seed id you provide.\\n\\nThe loop:\\n\\n    attn seed ready                  what you can pick up now: open, not parked, not blocked, nobody claiming it\\n                                     inside your plot when you report to one. Run it before you plant\\n    attn seed plant \\\"\u003ctitle\u003e\\\" -m \\\"…\\\" [--part-of \u003cplot\u003e] [--discovered-from \u003cseed\u003e]    a new seed; prints the id\\n\\n`tend`, `park`, `harvest`, `wither` and `replant` refuse a seed that another agent claims, and name that agent. Add `--force` to do it anyway. The log records that you forced it. A session's claim ends when the session ends.
